audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL logic (precompiled contracts, EVM stack operations, block validation, transaction processing, gas economics, block hash storage) and CL logic (voluntary exit processing and signature domain locking).

in_scope: Gas Economics (EIP-1559 base fee, access lists, refunds)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal trigger within the wallet provider, not an external entity. It represents an internal state change event, not data crossing a system boundary.

A calling contract within the EVM is an internal component of the Execution Layer. It operates within the same trust boundary as the precompile. Data flow from contract to precompile is an internal EVM call, not a trust boundary crossing.
The SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff..fe) is a privileged internal mechanism of the EL block processing pipeline. It is not an external entity but a synthetic internal caller.
Similar to EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT, a smart contract calling the history contract is an internal EVM operation, not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.
An abstract attacker model is not an external entity that sends data into the system. It is a threat actor concept, not a concrete data source.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any node can send blocks containing invalid headers, invalid PoW, or malformed transactions. All block data must be fully validated before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public JSON-RPC endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests. Users can submit malformed transactions, invalid signatures, or craft RPC queries to probe node behavior. No authentication required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via P2P/RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction pool ingestion (P2P gossip or JSON-RPC)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions arrive from unauthenticated sources. They may have invalid signatures, insufficient gas, incorrect nonces, or be crafted to exploit gas refund mechanisms. Full validation (intrinsic gas, sender recovery, nonce check, balance check) is mandatory.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Provider via web+evm:// Protocol
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser postMessage API via web+evm:// protocol handler
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any application can register a web+evm:// protocol handler. The wallet provider sends messages via browser postMessage which could be spoofed. Origin validation is required but not guaranteed. A malicious protocol handler could intercept wallet discovery and impersonate a legitimate wallet.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Extension via Browser Injection
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extensions inject provider objects into web page contexts. Any extension can inject itself; there is no authentication mechanism. Malicious extensions can emit false events, intercept RPC calls, or manipulate provider state. DApp clients must treat injected providers as untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client via Provider API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp clients attach event listeners to wallet providers. From the provider's perspective, any web page can attach listeners. Listener callbacks are untrusted code that could throw exceptions or behave maliciously.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web User via Block Explorer URL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP request with EIP-3091 standardized URL paths (/block/, /tx/, /address/, /token/)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web users provide URL path parameters that are directly used for data lookup. Path parameters could contain injection payloads (XSS, path traversal). Full input validation of block hashes, transaction hashes, and addresses is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blockchain Network via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network connectivity signals are not authenticated. Eclipse attacks can make the provider believe it is connected or disconnected. ChainId values received during connection must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Operator via Beacon P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain P2P gossip (voluntary exit messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Voluntary exit messages arrive via unauthenticated P2P gossip. While exits require a valid BLS signature, the message itself could be replayed, malformed, or submitted by any network participant (not necessarily the validator operator). Signature verification against the fixed Capella domain is mandatory. Cross-fork replay is intentionally allowed but must be understood.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via Beacon Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector: a malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or replay voluntary exits across forks. All validator-originated messages must be cryptographically verified.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious External Service via MEV-Boost Relay
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: External APIs (MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector: external services such as MEV-Boost relays or checkpoint sync providers can supply incorrect data, censor transactions, or perform denial of service. Data from these sources must be independently verified.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block header validation required: block number sequence, timestamp ordering, gas limit bounds, gas used <= gas limit, extra data size, parent hash integrity, difficulty calculation, and PoW verification. Any single validation failure must reject the entire block.

All RPC parameters must be validated: block hashes must be valid 32-byte hex, uncle indices must be within bounds, transaction bytes must decode to valid transaction types. Fork-dependent response fields (e.g., baseFee) must be conditionally included based on block height.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas sufficiency, sender address recovery from signature, nonce matching, balance sufficiency for gas + value, transaction type detection and proper decoding (legacy/EIP-2930/EIP-1559). Gas refund capped at 20% (London) or 50% (pre-London) of consumed gas. EIP-1559 transactions must have max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee.

Message origin must be verified before processing. ProviderInfo structure must be validated (required name and icon fields). MessagePort establishment must use the first valid response. RPC responses must contain exactly one of result or error. Messages with invalid origins must be discarded.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Browser extension content script injection point
boundary_edges.security_assumption: DApps must treat injected provider objects as untrusted. Provider-emitted events (connect, disconnect) carry chainId that must be independently verified. Multiple provider injections must be handled gracefully. Provider API calls may fail or return malicious data.

Listener callbacks are untrusted code. Exceptions thrown by one listener must not prevent invocation of others. Listener invocation order is not guaranteed. The provider must handle malicious listener behavior (infinite loops, resource exhaustion) gracefully.

URL path parameters must be validated for format (hex encoding, correct length) and sanitized against injection attacks (XSS, path traversal). Block hashes, transaction hashes, and addresses must match expected patterns. Non-existent resources must return 404, not error information that could leak internal state.

Network connectivity signals cannot be trusted. ChainId values must be verified via eth_chainId RPC when available. Connection/disconnection events must be emitted to all listeners regardless of individual listener failures. Eclipse attacks could manipulate perceived connectivity.

BLS signature must be verified against the fixed Capella fork domain (not current fork). Exit message fields (validator_index, epoch) must be validated. Cross-fork replay is intentionally permitted but the security model accepts this because exits only initiate the exit process and do not transfer funds. Exits signed with non-Capella domains must be rejected.

All validator-originated messages (blocks, attestations, voluntary exits) must be cryptographically verified. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Invalid block proposals must be rejected. Voluntary exit replay across forks is by design but limited to triggering exit (no fund transfer).

Data from external services must be independently verified against consensus rules. Checkpoint sync data must be validated against known finalized checkpoints. MEV-Boost relay responses must be verified before block proposal. Fallback to local block building must be available if relay is unavailable or returns invalid data.
